subject: Mid-cycle capacity bump & co-term credit request — Solstice Labs
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@solsticelabs.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@solsticelabs.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary capacity top-up + co-term

Hi Stephanie —

Quick note from our side: we’ve seen a 3x spike in inference usage for our document ingestion pipeline and will likely exceed the committed capacity for Q2. Can you share what a temporary top-up looks like (30–45 days) and whether we can (a) co-term the top-up to our annual renewal in September and (b) get a small promotional credit while legal finalizes the amendment?

I attached a short usage extract (Q2_usage_report.csv) to help with sizing. Procurement (cc’d) will need an estimate to speed internal approvals.

Thanks —
Maya
Sr. Platform Engineer
Solstice Labs
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@solsticelabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary capacity top-up + co-term

Thanks Maya — appreciate the heads up and the CSV. I pulled the usage and suggested a pragmatic path so you don’t hit throttles while keeping the renewal economics in mind. High level options:

- Short-term top-up (30 days) at 1.5x committed units: preserves your existing pricing; quick add-on amendment.
- Staged top-up (45 days) with 10% uplift credit applied at co-term if you annualize in Sept.
- Immediate capacity buffer with an execution credit (one-time) while legal circulates the amend — for teams with urgent latency sensitivity.

Can Ben outline the numbers and the discount/redemption mechanics? Irene, can you flag any operational gating for a 30–45 day staged add-on (billing/prorate implications)?

If that looks ok, I’ll send a short quote + amendment draft.

Best,
Steph
Director, Growth Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@solsticelabs.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary capacity top-up + co-term

Hi all —

Thanks for the context. Based on the Q2 extract, here are two concrete proposals (numbers are illustrative; final quote attached as redwood_uplift_quote_v2.pdf):

1) Rapid buffer (30 days)
- Units: +50% of monthly committed units for 30 days
- Rate: same unit price as current commitment
- One-time administrative fee: $1,250
- Legal: 1-page amendment; can be signed in 48 hours
- Credit: none (fastest path)

2) Staged uplift (45 days) -> co-term annualize in Sept
- Units: +75% of monthly committed units for 45 days
- Rate: current unit price less 8% uplift discount applied to the top-up portion if customer annualizes by Sept 30
- One-time admin fee: waived if annualize by Sept 30
- Redemption: 8% of invoiced top-up credited against first invoice post-annualization

Notes on mechanics:
- Billing will be pro-rated for the top-up period; accounting prefers a single invoice charged immediately to avoid month-end churn.
- Procurement note: if Solstice requires PO-first, we can provision with a PO in advance and invoice per the amendment.

Next steps: I’ve attached the quote and a redlined amendment template. If the staged uplift is acceptable, we’ll draft the canary amendment and send a DocuSign link for signature.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Maya Patel <maya@solsticelabs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@solsticelabs.com>, Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@solsticelabs.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary capacity top-up + co-term

Ben — thanks, that is helpful. A couple quick asks from our side:

- Can you soften the redemption so the credit applies even if we annualize within the next 120 days (rather than strictly Sept 30)? We have an internal approval lag and that flexibility would make procurement comfortable.
- Can the admin fee be applied as a credit if we hit a usage threshold during the top-up?

Procurement: we prefer a single invoice and will attach PO_88745. Tom (CFO) — if you’re ok, we can sign the amendment once the 120-day redemption window is confirmed.

Thanks —
Maya
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@solsticelabs.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T15:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary capacity top-up + co-term

Maya — appreciate the specificity. We can accommodate both asks with one guardrail: extend the redemption window to 120 days (from amendment effective date) and convert the admin fee into a credit if measured usage during the top-up exceeds the projected baseline by 40%. Summary of the final approach:

- Staged uplift (45 days) at +75% units
- 8% uplift discount on the top-up portion redeemable if customer annualizes within 120 days
- Admin fee ($1,250) credited back if actual top-up usage > projected baseline by 40%
- Single invoice up-front; PO_88745 accepted
- Legal: I’ll send the amended 1-page addendum with the 120-day window and the admin-fee credit clause.

Action items
- Ben: prepare the DocuSign with redwood_uplift_quote_v2.pdf and amendment (include credit language).
- Irene: confirm billing flow for single up-front invoice and PO acceptance.
- Maya / Procurement: confirm PO_88745 and sign when DocuSign link arrives.

I’ll also add a short note in HubSpot (HS-987654) to capture the concession. Thanks, all — we’ll keep this short and pragmatic so Solstice stays online without complicated invoicing.

Best,
Steph
Director, Growth Sales
Redwood Inference
